title: A Passage to India

vibeProfile.oneLine: An accusation in a cave shatters the fragile peace of colonial India.

summary: When a young Englishwoman accuses an Indian doctor of assaulting her in the Marabar Caves, the fragile courtesies between colonisers and colonised in British India collapse into a charged trial. Forster's masterpiece is a subtle, humane study of friendship, race and the impossibility of true understanding across the divide of empire. Set against the vast, indifferent Indian landscape, it is both a gripping human drama and one of the great novels about the moral failure of colonialism.
whyReadIt: Forster's masterpiece on the impossibility of friendship across the colonial divide. Humane, subtle and quietly damning.

funFacts.text: Forster drew on his own visits to India and never published another novel in his lifetime.
